description:
FILED s446l (agent L) from #502 probes; PRE-EXISTING.

REPRO: `print "[$^E]\n";` and `print "[$^C]\n";` -- perl prints the errno
string / 0; PCL aborts the whole program at LOAD with an unhandled
unbound-variable.  The emitted symbol is `|$^e|` (lower case): the name is not
in Pl/ExprToCL.pm's %SPECIAL_VARS, so it falls through to the ordinary global
path and gets case-INVERTED, which is also why the message reads `$^e`.

Every sibling caret variable IS there: $^A $^D $^F $^I $^L $^M $^N $^O $^P $^R
$^S $^T $^V $^W $^X $^H.  $^E and $^C are simply missing -- 39 of the 45
punctuation/caret names probed in s446l work.

FIX (measured, small): two entries in %SPECIAL_VARS (Pl/ExprToCL.pm ~251) plus
the runtime side.
  $^E on POSIX IS $!  -- probed: after a failed open, perl gives the identical
     string for both -- so the right mapping is the SAME one $! has,
     ['p-errno-string'], not a new inert defvar (an inert cell would read ""
     after a failed syscall = silent wrong).
  $^C is 0 at run time always (PCL has no -c), so a `(defvar |$^C| (make-p-box 0))`
     + export is exact.
This is a Pl/ EMISSION change (generation bump + artifact regeneration) plus a
cl/ change (full sweep), which is why s446l routed lib/English.pm around it
instead: $EXTENDED_OS_ERROR is served by the errno tie and $COMPILING is set to
0.  Doing this task lets both become ordinary aliases.

BAR: read + write + numeric context for $^E vs perl after a failed syscall;
$^C read; the 39 working siblings unchanged; corpus-diff (expected IDENTICAL --
no corpus file names either).


DONE s448o (Opus, agent O of round 6), commit 97b10b6 (rebased).

Shipped exactly as the task measured it: `'$^E' => ['p-errno-string']` and
`'$^C' => '|$^C|'` in %SPECIAL_VARS (Pl/ExprToCL.pm), plus
`(defvar |$^C| (make-p-box 0))` and its export in cl/pcl-runtime.lisp.

$^E's mapping re-probed in BOTH directions before shipping: set $! and read
$^E, set $^E and read $!, numeric context both ways, and the string after a
failed open -- perl and PCL now byte-identical on all of it.  An inert cell
would have read "" after a failed syscall, which is the silent wrong the task
warned about.

lib/English.pm's `our $COMPILING = 0` became the ordinary alias
`*COMPILING = \$^C` its neighbours already are (probed: writing either name is
visible through the other, as in perl).  $EXTENDED_OS_ERROR KEEPS its errno
tie: $^E is an ACCESSOR, not a cell, so perl's `\$^E` spelling would take a
reference to a temporary box instead of aliasing.  Nothing in either population
uses English, so that shim change cannot move a sweep row.
docs/not-supported.md's English section rewritten -- it said both names had no
runtime variable, which this task makes false.

REACH, measured: in-repo, exactly one file names $^E or $^C (lib/English.pm).
In perl's t/, five do -- t/base/rs.t, t/op/hash-clear-placeholders.t,
t/op/hash-rt85026.t, t/loc_tools.pl, t/win32/signal.t -- and every one reads
$^E only in an error branch, which is why they were not already dying: an
unbound special is a RUN-time error in SBCL, so the abort only happens on the
path that names it.  Three cpan-tests modules name $^C
(Test/Builder.pm, Test/Tester/Capture.pm, Test2/Formatter/TAP.pm) and their
emission changes, which is why the generation bump was required.

Guard Pl/t/caret-vars-01.t rows 3-5.  FILED: #601 (perl's $^C STORE is
(bool)SvIV, so `$^C = 5` reads 1 there and 5 here -- the whole flag-shaped
caret family needs one measurement before anyone writes a magic cell).
subject: $^E and $^C have no runtime variable: naming either ABORTS with an unbound CL variable (`The variable $^e is unbound`)
